result.topic_en: Opening of a chapter on determining the Moon's position from lunar eclipses, arguing that eclipse observations are the best data for fixing the mean longitude, anomaly, node and eccentricity because they are free of parallax.
result.transcription:
XVI.

Tria Capita ex Opere quodam majori inedito
de theoria lunae.

Caput ....
De loco lunae ex eclipsibus lunaribus determinando.

§ 1. Quo ex formulis hactenus inventis, quibus motus lunae continetur, ad quodvis tempus verus lunae locus in coelo definiri possit, primum aliquot ejus loca cognita esse oportet, ut deinceps tam longitudo media lunae quam ejus anomalia et locus nodi ad illa loca accommodari, ac praeterea vera excentricitas lunae exacte determinari possit. Si enim luna in motu suo eas sequatur regulas, quas ex theoria elicuimus, certum est, si formulae inventae ad aliquot loca observata accommodentur, eas perpetuo cum observationibus congruere debere. Ad hoc ergo institutum ejusmodi observationes eligi conveniet, ex quibus verus lunae locus geocentricus accurate concludi queat, ut ne quidem ejus parallaxi sit opus, quippe quae postquam theoria penitus fuerit confirmata, demum exacte assignari poterit. Nullius ergo etiamnunc erunt usus neque observationes culminationis lunae, neque occultationes stellarum fixarum, quoniam ex iis sine cognita parallaxi verum lunae locum concludere non licet.

§ 2. Ad praesentem ergo scopum observationes eclipsium lunae sine dubio erunt aptissimae, quae ubivis terrarum, ubi quidem lunam conspicere licet, eaedem apparent, neque a varietate parallaxeos inquinantur. Eveniunt autem hujusmodi eclipses circa oppositionem lunae et solis, in iisque datur temporis momentum, quo longitudo lunae e diametro opponitur longitudini solis: quod momentum si esset cognitum, quoniam pro eo locum solis definire liceret, hinc facillime vera longitudo lunae concludi posset. Verum hoc ipsum momentum verae oppositionis in observatione non ita distincte exprimitur, sed demum ex comparatione reliquarum circumstantiarum non obvio ratiocinio concludi potest. Quae enim in quavis eclipsi lunae attenta observatione distinguere licet, sunt ejus initium et finis; tum, si eclipsis fuerit totalis, momentum immersionis integrae et initium emersionis.

items.quote: Quo ex formulis hactenus inventis, quibus motus lunae continetur, ad quodvis tempus verus lunae locus in coelo definiri possit, primum aliquot ejus loca cognita esse oportet, ut deinceps tam longitudo media lunae quam ejus anomalia et locus nodi ad illa loca accommodari, ac praeterea vera excentricitas lunae exacte determinari possit.
items.english: So that from the formulas found so far, which contain the motion of the Moon, the true place of the Moon in the sky can be determined for any time, some of its places must first be known, so that thereafter both the mean longitude of the Moon and its anomaly and the place of the node can be fitted to those places, and moreover the true eccentricity of the Moon can be exactly determined.

items.quote: Si enim luna in motu suo eas sequatur regulas, quas ex theoria elicuimus, certum est, si formulae inventae ad aliquot loca observata accommodentur, eas perpetuo cum observationibus congruere debere.
items.english: For if the Moon in its motion follows the rules we have derived from theory, it is certain that, if the formulas found are fitted to some observed places, they must always agree with the observations.

items.quote: Ad praesentem ergo scopum observationes eclipsium lunae sine dubio erunt aptissimae, quae ubivis terrarum, ubi quidem lunam conspicere licet, eaedem apparent, neque a varietate parallaxeos inquinantur.
items.english: For the present purpose, therefore, observations of lunar eclipses will without doubt be the most suitable, since they appear the same everywhere on Earth where the Moon can be seen, and are not contaminated by variation of parallax.

items.quote: Verum hoc ipsum momentum verae oppositionis in observatione non ita distincte exprimitur, sed demum ex comparatione reliquarum circumstantiarum non obvio ratiocinio concludi potest.
items.english: But this very moment of true opposition is not so distinctly shown in the observation; it can only be inferred, by no obvious reasoning, from a comparison of the other circumstances.
